## What it is
A **mature, stalled full-stack hosted web app** — not a sketch. `apps/web` Next.js 16 + IBM Carbon + Monaco; `apps/api` FastAPI + Firestore on Cloud Run + Firebase Hosting, email/password auth, per-user data. 91 commits (Jan–Jun 2026), ~400 files, Playwright + Vitest, OpenSpec-driven. **Momentum stalled ~2026-06-26** mid "Chat Parity Sprint" (`dev/fufo-chat-parity`); the roadmap's last two items (LangChain/LangGraph targets, App Hosting deploy) never shipped.

Same **problem** (curate → version → assemble primitives → compile to harnesses) and literally the **same two primary targets** (`claude_code`, `opencode`). Diverges on substrate: **Firestore DB records + a runtime REST build pipeline + hosted multi-user GUI** vs **git flat files + deterministic generators + drift guards + a CLI/CI plugin marketplace**. ## Problem
`primitives-core/` is defined as "the single source copy of every **primitive**" (flow node `primitive-bodies`). A **bundle** is an *assembly/composition config* (which primitives group into a plugin), not a primitive itself. Nesting `primitives-core/bundles/` under the primitives source blurs that line — Henry flagged it directly.

## Blast radius (flow-DAG-touching)
`primitives-core/bundles/{code-desk,diagrams,exec-desk,foreman-kit,obsidian-toolkit}` is read by: `scripts/gen_marketplace.py`, `tests/test_gen_marketplace.py`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `primitives-core/README.md`, `evals/ingest.py`, `scripts/check_identity.py`, plus the `primitive-bodies` flow node note. A move must update all of them + add a `bundles/` (or `assemblies/`) top-level flow node and re-run `make flow`.

## Options
- **A (recommended): top-level `bundles/`** with its own flow node (layer `roster`). Cleanest separation: primitives = parts, bundles = assembly configs. One sequenced wave (shares flow.yaml + the generator with NOTE-d).
- **B: rename in place** to `primitives-core/_bundles/` or similar — cheaper, keeps the coupling, weaker signal.
- **C: leave it** — the coupling is tolerable; close as wontfix.

## Recommendation
A. It matches the mental model the repo already documents (roster + dist lanes) and the functionform-asmbl "parts vs assemblies" framing. Needs Henry's sign-off (major IA change).

## What

Package the three BuilderIO visual-planning skills — **`visual-plan`**,
**`visual-recap`**, **`visualize-repo`** — as a distributable dotfiles-agents
plugin bundle (a cross-desk standalone), so any repo can enable them via
`claude plugin enable` instead of copying `.claude/skills/` files per-repo.

## Why

They currently live committed per-repo — source of truth is
`hsb3/agent-native-sandbox` `.claude/skills/{visual-plan,visual-recap,visualize-repo}/`.
Each new repo needs a manual `npx @agent-native/skills add … --scope project`
install (procedure in that repo's `_meta/reference/skills-setup.md`). Onboarding
them to the marketplace gives the standard deny-by-default + per-project
`claude plugin enable` path and one canonical copy to maintain instead of N repo copies.

## Composition — what's Henry's vs upstream

- **Upstream (BuilderIO):** the skill bodies + `references/*.md` (canvas,
  wireframe, document-quality, exemplar, connection, local-files). Installed via
  `npx @agent-native/skills@latest add`.
- **Henry's override:** only the `## Installed Mode` preamble in each `SKILL.md`.
  It points the workflow at the **local Plan app container**
  `ghcr.io/hsb3/plan-app` (private) instead of the unreliable hosted bridge, and
  is now **machine-portable** — GHCR login derived from the GitHub session, the
  Anthropic key optional + env-driven, rendering/editing need no secrets. See
  agent-native-sandbox commit `caeb176`.

## Deliverables

- A plugin bundle (proposed name `visual-planning`; `plan-app` also a candidate)
  under the dotfiles-agents marketplace, containing the 3 skills + their `references/`.
- The portable `Installed Mode` preamble carried as the canonical override.
- A **re-sync procedure**: re-pull an upstream BuilderIO skill update and
  re-apply the preamble overlay without losing it — the maintenance crux, since
  the bodies are upstream and only the preamble is ours.
- Marketplace registration + a plugin README (per the #144 README-coverage convention).
- A migration note: what supersedes the per-repo `skills-setup.md` install for
  Henry's own repos, and the tradeoff kept (per-repo committed = travels with the
  repo for collaborators who clone; plugin = user/machine-scoped).

## Acceptance criteria

- `claude plugin enable visual-planning@dotfiles-agents` in a fresh repo surfaces
  `/visual-plan`, `/visual-recap`, `/visualize-repo`.
- Running one authors a plan that renders in the container on any Apple-Silicon
  machine logged into GitHub (the portability contract from the source repo), with
  no per-machine secret tooling.
- The re-sync procedure is documented and demonstrated once (an upstream update
  pulled, preamble preserved).

## Open questions

- **Placement** — standalone cross-desk plugin (per the #134 desk-set restructure
  vocabulary) vs attached to a desk. These are cross-cutting, not desk-specific →
  lean standalone.
- **Private-image coupling** — the bundle is not self-contained: it depends on the
  private `ghcr.io/hsb3/plan-app` + GHCR read access. Acceptable for a personal
  marketplace; document the prerequisite. (Image stays private; the owner flips it
  to public manually when proven — do not surface publishing as a task.)
- **Upstream drift** — cadence for re-pulling BuilderIO skill updates, and whether
  to pin a known-good upstream skills version.

## References

- Source skills: `hsb3/agent-native-sandbox` `.claude/skills/{visual-plan,visual-recap,visualize-repo}/`
- Portability contract + preamble: agent-native-sandbox commit `caeb176`;
  `_meta/reference/skills-setup.md`; `_meta/reference/plan-app-docker.md`
- Related: dotfiles-agents #134/#135 (desk-set restructure), #144 (plugin README coverage)
title: plugin: visual-planning — onboard visual-plan/visual-recap/visualize-repo as a distributable bundle

## Context

The repo's work product is **primitives** (skills/agents/hooks) authored in `primitives-core/`, tracked in the `primitives-core.yaml` roster, and assembled into `plugins/` + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` by `scripts/gen_marketplace.py` (`make build`), gated by `make ci`. The rules that govern authoring — edit `primitives-core/` only, regenerate (never hand-edit generated trees), the roster schema, identity-neutrality, provenance, hook layout, stdlib-only tests, branch-off-`dev`/PR-into-`dev` — currently live **only in agent-facing docs** (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `primitives-core/README.md`).

Two gaps:

1. **No human-facing `CONTRIBUTING.md`.** A contributor — or a future agent onboarding cold — has no single entry doc for the workflow and invariants. The knowledge exists but is scattered across agent digests.
2. **No skill that operationalizes creating the repo's own work product.** The marketplace ships skills for authoring *other* repos' structure (`mise-en-place-scaffold`, `repo-meta-structure`, `planning-desk`), but nothing that scaffolds/authors a new *primitive for this marketplace* to standard — a conformant roster entry, the right directory layout, passing `--check` drift guards and tests. Dogfooding gap: the repo that produces authoring skills has no authoring skill for itself.

## Deliverables

**A. `CONTRIBUTING.md`** (root or `.github/`) — distills, does not duplicate, the canonical rules (links to `CLAUDE.md` / `primitives-core/README.md` as source of truth):
- the contribution loop: branch off `dev` → edit `primitives-core/` only → `make build` → `make ci` → PR into `dev` (`main` is publish-only)
- the source-of-truth rule (generated `plugins/` / `marketplace.json` are never hand-edited)
- the roster (`primitives-core.yaml`) entry schema + `origin: authored|sourced` rule
- the invariants `make ci` enforces: roster↔disk, identity-neutrality, provenance, hook layout, stdlib-only tests
- how to run the gate locally (`make ci`, `make help`)

**B. An authoring skill** (or an extension of an existing one) for the repo's work product:
- scaffold a new primitive (skill / agent / hook) with a conformant `primitives-core/<type>/<id>/` layout + roster entry, then `make build` + `make ci` to green
- survey overlap first: `repo-meta-structure` / `mise-en-place-scaffold` cover generic repo meta-structure, not marketplace-primitive authoring — confirm the boundary before adding vs. extending
- decide whether this is one "author-a-primitive" skill or a thin "contribution-loop" skill (edit → build → ci → PR); recommend in the plan

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, links to (does not copy) the canonical agent docs, and a newcomer can follow it to land a primitive
- [ ] The contribution loop and every `make ci` invariant are documented with the exact commands
- [ ] A decision is recorded (issue comment or ADR) on the authoring-skill shape — new skill vs. extend `mise-en-place-scaffold` / `repo-meta-structure` — with the overlap boundary stated
- [ ] If a new skill: it is rostered (`origin: authored`), builds clean, and `make ci` stays green
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` gain a one-line pointer to `CONTRIBUTING.md` (no duplication)

## Notes

- The standing rule is "don't add a CONTRIBUTING file unless specifically requested" — this issue **is** that request.
- Scope is additive; no change to the generate/gate pipeline.
title: Add CONTRIBUTING.md + an authoring skill for the repo's own work product (primitives)

## Why

The marketplace now distributes 7 plugins (post-#134 restructure), but only the two desk bundles (`code-desk`, `exec-desk`) ship a README. Five distributed plugins have none: **foreman-kit, github-project-board, opencode-expertise, pptx-themes, private-fork**. There is also no in-repo inventory of what the marketplace offers — a consumer (or Henry) has to read `marketplace.json` raw.

## Deliverables

**D1 — Generated plugin inventory.** A repo-level inventory of every distributed plugin (name, kind — bundle / plugin / standalone skill —, version, one-line description, contents summary: skills/agents/hooks count or list, install command `claude plugin install <id>@dotfiles-agents`). Emitted by `gen_marketplace.py` (sole marketplace owner) as a generated artifact — either a `PLUGINS.md` or a clearly-marked generated section of the root README — with a drift guard in the existing check lanes (red-able: hand-edit → CI fails).

**D2 — README for every distributed plugin.** Author README sources for the five missing plugins in the established value/proof register (what you get, worked example, honest scope — match `code-desk`/`exec-desk`):
- `foreman-kit` — the delegation kit: foreman + handoff skills, scout/builder/reviewer/lead agents, 4 discipline hooks
- `github-project-board`, `private-fork`, `opencode-expertise`, `pptx-themes` — standalone one-skill plugins (README can be brief: what the skill does, when it triggers, install line)

**D3 — Coverage guard.** A check that every plugin in `marketplace.json` ships a `plugins/<id>/README.md` (red-able by removing one).

## Constraints (binding)

- Generated artifacts never hand-edited; `gen_marketplace.py` assembles READMEs from source files (extend the D8a bundle-README mechanism to plugin/standalone kinds).
- **The standalone wrappers are guarded byte-identical to their skill source** (`check_skill_catalog` / standalone-wrapper check). Adding a README into a wrapper dir must extend that guard's contract deliberately (e.g. wrapper = skill source + assembled README, README excluded from the byte-identity scope) — not weaken it.
- Identity neutrality per the entry-gate floor; the `author` manifest attribution exception stands. README bodies neutral.
- `make ci` green; all guards red-able.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All 7 `plugins/<id>/README.md` exist in the generated tree and regenerate zero-drift.
2. The inventory artifact lists exactly the marketplace lineup, regenerates zero-drift, and CI fails if either goes stale.
3. Standalone-wrapper byte-identity guard still red-able on a real source mutation.
4. `make ci` fully green.

## Provenance

Henry's ask 2026-07-18 (post-cutover). Desk fact-check on `main`@`44f643b3`: README present = code-desk, exec-desk; missing = the five above. Built by the desk-supervised native crew, one PR into `dev`; publish to `main` owner-gated.

2. **Anything that spans both desks ships STANDALONE** — its own plugin or catalog skill, never a member of a desk bundle.

> **Tracking:** owner directive 2026-07-12 ("there are a lot of skills in primitives-core/skills
> written by not me that we need to address — audit all items"). Full-roster provenance audits ran
> 2026-07-12 (old desk) and 2026-07-14 (executive desk, adversarially verified); this issue carries
> the remediation. Owner approved filing and ruled the open questions 2026-07-14 (desk decision
> 0005, under explicit delegation).

## What the audits found (65 items, re-verified 2026-07-14)

- **22 of 65 primitives are roster-labeled `origin: sourced`** — third-party content stored INSIDE
  `primitives-core/`: the 10 langchain-stack skills (langchain-ai), 4 openspec skills (Fission-AI),
  3 deep-agents skills (langchain-ai), framework-selection (langchain-ai), shadcn (shadcn-ui),
  skill-creator (anthropics), find-skills (vercel-labs), devcontainer-setup (trailofbits). All 22
  labels are truthful (real upstream + pinned ref).
- **Correction to the 2026-07-12 audit:** two vendored items DO hide in the `authored` set —
  **carbon-builder** (adapted from IBM Carbon Design System's skill; retains Apache-2.0, and
  `SKILL.md` says "adapted from an MCP-backed original") and **nanobanana** (vendored from
  `GargantuaX/openskills`; its README is the upstream's own, install command points there).
  **react-doctor** is unclear (21-line wrapper around the `react-doctor` npm tool; no upstream
  skill file located). Effective third-party scope: **24 confirmed + 1 unclear**.
- **Four plugins are 100% third-party content** (langchain-stack, openspec, deep-agents, meta);
  frontend-extras is half (shadcn).
- **The governing rule was undefined at charter level** — CLAUDE.md's "tracked, not vendored"
  language vs the sourced-in-core practice. Resolved by the owner ruling below.

## The ruled boundary (owner decision, 2026-07-14 — deliverable A codifies it)

1. **`origin: sourced` in `primitives-core/` is reserved for adopted forks we intentionally
   maintain and diverge**, each with a recorded divergence rationale. Everything tracked verbatim
   moves to `externals.yaml` by reference once #36 (clone-at-build) lands; until then items stay
   physically put and the ADR states the intent.
2. **Agent-generated content produced under the owner's direction is self-authored** for
   provenance purposes. Whether those items earn distribution is a usage question owned by the
   business-case retrofit / plugin-lineup ruling, not this issue.

## Deliverables

- **A — the boundary ADR** (`docs/decisions/`): codify the ruled boundary above. Charter gets a
  one-line pointer; CLAUDE.md/CHARTER language reconciled.
- **B — per-item disposition for all 24 confirmed third-party items (+ resolve react-doctor)**
  applying the ADR: adopt-as-fork (divergence rationale recorded) | move to externals (depends
  on #36) | retire to the salvage pile. Includes relabeling the two mislabels (carbon-builder →
  sourced/adapted with vendor + upstream; nanobanana → sourced with vendor + upstream) and a
  provenance verdict for react-doctor. Recorded on the roster (coordinate the mechanism with #39).
- **C — upstream-drift cadence:** pinned refs go stale silently; define the recurring upstream
  review step (the private-fork skill's upstream-review cycle is the SOP model) for whatever
  stays vendored.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The ADR exists, is Accepted, matches the ruled boundary, and CLAUDE.md/CHARTER language
      agrees with it (no more tracked-not-vendored vs sourced-in-core contradiction).
- [ ] All 24 confirmed third-party items have a recorded disposition and react-doctor has a
      resolved verdict; `make ci` and the sourced-entry guard stay green through any moves.
- [ ] carbon-builder and nanobanana roster entries carry truthful `origin`/vendor/upstream fields.
- [ ] Items moved to externals render identically from `externals.yaml` (`make build` drift
      guard proves it) or are explicitly retired with their plugin membership updated.
- [ ] The upstream-review cadence is written where the curation loop will actually hit it
      (workbench lifecycle docs or the roster README), not a flat note.

## Dependencies & gates

- Depends on: #36 (clone-at-build externals) for any move-to-externals disposition; coordinates
  with #39 (roster provenance field) and the sibling plugin business-case retrofit proposal
  (whether langchain-stack / openspec / deep-agents / meta earn distribution at all is ITS
  question; this issue owns where their content lives).
- Gates: `make ci` (roster guard, validate, build drift); ADR discipline per project protocol.

body:
> **Tracking:** #99, owner directive 2026-07-12 ("the broad ignore policy seems to create quite a
> few issues"). Decide-first: evaluate the `_meta/` broad-ignore + negation gitignore policy, pick a
> successor, amend the repo-meta-structure STANDARD it comes from, then migrate this repo + adopters.

## Problem

The `_meta/` gitignore policy is ignore-by-default (`_meta/*`) with tracked items re-included by
negation. The stanza has grown to 27 lines (`.gitignore:16-42`) and the pattern keeps biting:

- **Negation fragility.** Every tracked subtree needs paired `!dir/` + `!dir/**` lines, each
  re-inclusion re-admits Finder/Python litter past the global rules (4 extra `.DS_Store` rules at
  `.gitignore:24-25,30-31,41-42`; the `__pycache__` section must stay ORDERED after the negations,
  `.gitignore:44`), and the base ignore must be the `_meta/*` form or negations silently fail
  (git cannot negate inside a wholly-ignored directory). 18 compliance rows (IGNORE-01..18) exist
  largely to police this fragility.
- **Content invisible where it is needed.** `_meta/research/` is gitkeep-only (`.gitignore:37`):
  the 2026-07-12 ecosystem survey could not be linked from the owner's decision brief (delivered
  as a file attachment instead), and research is invisible to worktree agents and lost on clone.
  `_meta/NOTE.md` (ignored via `.gitignore:17`) held the idea list that spawned #48/#49 — load-bearing
  content in an ignored file.
- **Tracked-by-negation still needs manual discipline.** Briefings flipped to fully-tracked
  2026-07-05, but folders sit untracked until someone remembers to `git add` (the wave-decisions
  rulings brief sat untracked for a day; the 2026-07-12 governance brief is untracked now).
  Ignore policy and commit discipline are entangled.
- **The policy is a packaged STANDARD, not just this repo's file.** The stanza is defined by
  repo-meta-structure (`primitives-core/skills/repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md`
  IGNORE rows), seeded by mise-en-place-scaffold, measured by repo-compliance-audit, and already
  enacted in adopters (workbench, fleet-dashboard pilot #33). Changing it here without amending
  the standard recreates the CLAUDE.md-vs-charter drift the third-party-disposition proposal
  just flagged.

## Deliverables

- **A — evaluation + decision (ADR in `docs/decisions/`).** Compare at least: (1) status quo
  broad-ignore + negation; (2) track-by-default inside `_meta/` with targeted ignores only
  (`operations/`, caches, OS litter); (3) relocating the secret-holding dir out of `_meta/` so the
  whole desk tracks cleanly. The ADR states the chosen policy and the secret-safety argument.
- **B — this repo migrated.** `.gitignore` rewritten to the chosen policy; a pre-flip secrets scan
  of everything newly tracked (operations/ content must remain untracked under every option);
  existing local-only content (research docs, NOTE.md) explicitly committed or explicitly ruled
  local, none left ambiguous.
- **C — the standard amended in the same change.** repo-meta-structure reference + IGNORE checklist
  rows + the mise-en-place-scaffold gitignore template + the planning-desk setup instructions all
  updated together; `make ci` drift guards prove the packaged skills regenerate.
- **D — adopter migration notes.** A short apply note for workbench + fleet-dashboard (and the
  memory-hygiene stanza in the dotfiles instructions that mirrors this pattern).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The ADR exists and is Accepted; the policy statement appears in exactly one canonical place,
      and repo-meta-structure / CLAUDE.md / scaffold template all point at it without contradiction.
- [ ] `git check-ignore` behavior on this repo matches the ADR for every `_meta/` subtree; a
      secrets scan of the newly tracked set is clean; `_meta/operations/` content remains ignored.
- [ ] The compliance audit's IGNORE rows are updated to test the NEW policy and pass on this repo
      and the workbench (no orphaned rows testing the old pattern).
- [ ] Research artifacts cited by comm packages are clone-survivable (linkable on GitHub) or the
      ADR explicitly rules them local — the 2026-07-12 brief's attachment workaround cannot recur
      silently.
- [ ] `make ci` green: roster/targets drift guards prove the amended skills regenerated.

## Dependencies & gates

- Sequencing: coordinates with the ruled toolkit wave (#68 -> #83 -> #82) — #82 renames
  `_meta/plans/` -> `_meta/issues/` and edits the SAME standard files; land this before or after
  #82, not interleaved.
- Related: #33 (pilot re-audit consumes the updated IGNORE rows), #69/#70 (sibling standards
  fixes), the third-party-disposition proposal (same one-canonical-rule discipline).
- Gates: `make ci` (validate + names + build drift); ADR discipline per project protocol;
  compliance audit green on both repos post-change.

## Open owner decisions

1. **The successor policy** — recommended default: option 2 (track-by-default inside `_meta/`
   with explicit ignores for `operations/`, caches, and OS litter), which deletes most of the
   negation machinery and makes new desk content clone-survivable without per-subtree ceremony.
2. **Whether `_meta/operations/` stays inside `_meta/`** (option 3 moves it out entirely so no
   secret-holding path lives under a tracked-by-default tree).
title: chore: evaluate + replace the _meta/ broad-ignore gitignore policy (standard + repo + adopters)

> **Tracking:** #79, portability audit 2026-07-04 (fresh-machine session on the second MacBook surfaced machine-tied assumptions across all four primitive types); companion gate issue: workbench#32. Primitives must not assume any one machine's state; dependencies become a declared, checkable contract.

## Problem

Primitives were authored on one machine and silently assume its state. A full sweep of `primitives-core/` (audit session 2026-07-04) found three defect classes, none of which any current guard catches:

1. **Assumed-installed binaries.** All 4 MCP specs (`agent-bus`, `audio`, `deck-builder`, `excalidraw`) reference custom stdio binaries with zero install provenance — `primitives-core/mcp/README.md:17` documents `command` as "bare command — resolved on PATH (portable; no machine paths)", which assumes the binary exists and gives dotfiles-bootstrap nothing to act on. Skills likewise: `diagrams/SKILL.md:21-23` (`apt-get install -y graphviz`, `pip install --break-system-packages` — Linux-only + non-standard), `obsidian-cli/SKILL.md:20` (hardcoded `/Applications/Obsidian.app/...`), `memory-taxonomy/SKILL.md:14` (`cc-project-memory` with no source stated), `setup-project-dashboard/SKILL.md:51` (`speak_gemini`), `pptx-henry/scripts/render-pptx.sh:30` (`pdftoppm` + LibreOffice/PowerPoint, macOS-only).
2. **Machine/user-specific state.** `memory-taxonomy/SKILL.md:23-24` points at the `hsb-2026` Obsidian vault path as the authoritative design doc; `comms/references/comm-package-standard.md:14,22,37` hardcodes `~/Developer/fleet-dashboard`, `~/.claude/skills/pptx-henry/assets/theme-tokens.js`, and states the work GitHub account as `mhi-acme` (a client-token scrub left a factually wrong account name).
3. **No dependency contract.** The roster's `requires:` vocabulary is `hooks|local-mcp|hosted-mcp` only (`scripts/check_roster.py:9`) and exactly one entry uses it (`comms`). There is no way to declare "this primitive needs binary X / machine state Y", so nothing can check or provision it.

The hooks half of the problem (inline prompts in `dev-focus/hooks/hooks.json`, config/script split) is enforced by the new checks here; the gate-side rules land in the sibling workbench issue.

Why the guards missed it: the workbench gate's H5 scans only the literal `/Users/henry` (`dotfiles-agents-workbench/scripts/promote_check.py:215`), and all 84 roster entries are `grandfathered-pending-use` (promotions log, 2026-07-03 Q-13 record) — they never faced even that narrow check. This repo's `validate_primitives.py` has no portability checks at all.

## Deliverables

- A — **Roster schema: dependency grammar.** Extend `requires:` with `cli:<kebab>` (a binary/app that must be installed) and `env:<kebab>` (machine state, e.g. `env:dotfiles`), keeping the three existing capability words. Grammar validated in `scripts/check_roster.py`; documented in the `primitives-core.yaml` header and `primitives-core/README.md`.
- B — **MCP spec schema: install provenance.** A required `install:` block for stdio specs (`upstream` repo/URL + `install` command) in `primitives-core/mcp/README.md` schema, enforced by `scripts/validate_primitives.py`.
- C — **Mirror checks in `make ci`** (`scripts/validate_primitives.py` + tests): (1) machine-path scan over `primitives-core/` — `/Users/`, `~/` and `$HOME` paths outside the primitive's own tree, `/Applications/`, vault names, `apt-get install`, `--break-system-packages`; (2) undeclared-dependency scan — references to a maintained machine-local tool registry (custom `~/.local/bin` scripts, custom MCP binaries) must be covered by the entry's `requires:`; (3) hook config hygiene — `hooks.json` command values must be handler references (no inline scripts), inline prose (prompts/args) capped at 20 words.
- D — **In-place fixes** for: `diagrams` (portable per-platform install), `obsidian-cli` (per-platform binary resolution), `comms` references (resolve dashboard/theme paths at runtime; fix the account name), `memory-taxonomy` (genericize the vault pointer), `setup-project-dashboard` (declare `speak_gemini` optional with provenance), `pptx-henry` (per-platform prereqs section), `dotfiles-expert` (declare `requires: [env:dotfiles]` — domain-scoped by design, not demoted).
- E — **Demotions.** Remove the 4 MCP entries + the 2 `dev-focus.*` hook entries from the roster; move files to `dotfiles-agents-workbench/incubator/`; demotion records in the workbench promotions log citing this issue; the `dev-focus` plugin ships skill-only until the hooks re-qualify; `make build` regenerates targets.
- F — **`requires:` declarations** added across remaining entries wherever the new scan detects a dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

Found 2026-07-04 while running the board overhaul on a real org project (mhi-raptorxai project #5), project-workflow plugin 0.2.1.

## Bug
`skills/github-project-board/scripts/*.py` share a `graphql()` helper that passes every variable with `gh api graphql -f k=v`. `-f` is always a **string** field, but the queries declare typed variables (`$n:Int!` in `PROJECT_ID_Q`, etc.), so current `gh` fails with:

```
gh: Variable $n of type Int! was provided invalid value
```

This breaks `board-export.py`, `board-apply.py`, and `board-fields.py` on first contact — the whole export→analyze→apply loop is dead until patched.

## Fix
One character in the shared helper — use `-F` (typed: coerces numbers/booleans, leaves strings alone) for variables; keep `-f` for the query text itself:

```python
def graphql(query: str, **fvars: str) -> dict:
    args = ["api", "graphql", "-f", "query=" + query]
    for k, v in fvars.items():
        args += ["-F", f"{k}={v}"]   # was -f
```

Verified: with this patch all three scripts ran clean against the org project (92-item export, 384-row changeset applied, idempotent re-run 0 changed).

## Two adjacent paper cuts from the same session (fold in or split, your call)
1. **Changeset header row:** `board-apply.py` requires the `issue<TAB>field<TAB>value` header (documented in the docstring) and silently plans `0 changed · 0 unchanged · 0 skipped` on a headerless file — a headerless TSV looks like a successful no-op. Consider exiting non-zero when zero rows parse, and/or telling the board-analyst agent prompt to always emit the header (the bundled analyst produced headerless TSVs).
2. **`--owner-type` default is `user`:** on an org project the failure surfaces as the (misleading) Int! error above rather than "project not found". After the -F fix the error becomes the proper `project not found (check --owner-type)` message, so this mostly resolves itself — noting for test coverage.

## Repro
```bash
python3 skills/github-project-board/scripts/board-export.py -o <org> -n <N> --owner-type org
# before patch: gh: Variable $n of type Int! was provided invalid value
```

## What happened

Real-world use in `mhi-raptorxai/raptorxai-infra` (2026-07-03): a fresh desk was scaffolded and three `issue-body.md` files were staged per the skill's own issue mode (bodies first, `plan.md` later). The governance toolkit could not see them:

- `reconcile.py` header reported `(3 active rows, 0 archived, 0 folders)` and emitted `DRIFT [row-no-folder] ... ACTIVE row has no plan folder on disk` — while the folders existed on disk with staged `issue-body.md` files.
- `sync-bodies.py` reported `Sync _meta/plans/*/issue-body.md vs GitHub (0 folders)` and compared nothing, even after the bodies were published as live issues #1-#3. Its stated purpose ("each folder's issue-body.md vs the live GitHub body") silently doesn't apply to any folder lacking `plan.md`.

Root cause: `disk_folders()` in `reconcile.py` (and the equivalent in `sync-bodies.py`) defines a plan folder as `(p / "plan.md").is_file()`.

## Why it matters

The skill's own workflow produces issue-body-only folders as a normal intermediate state (issue mode explicitly ships `issue-body.md` as the contract, with `plan.md` authored later "if the work needs build detail"). In that state the toolkit is blind: reconcile emits a misleading drift kind (`row-no-folder` for a folder that exists), and sync-bodies gives false assurance (0 differ) while staged bodies could drift from live issues unchecked.

Workaround used: kept such folders out of the ACTIVE table and invented a "PUBLISHED, plan pending" list in the README prose — which also reveals the README schema has no documented home for the staged-not-filed and published-no-plan lifecycle states.

## Suggested direction

- Count a folder with either artifact; distinguish `plan.md missing` (warn) from `folder missing` (drift).
- Make `sync-bodies.py` key on `issue-body.md` presence (that's the artifact it diffs).
- Give the plans-README template a documented state for pre-plan rows (or bless the prose-list pattern).

Observed with planning-desk from plugin cache 0.1.0 while repo-compliance-audit ran from 0.2.1 (mixed-version cache — separate note in the other issues). If 0.2.1+ already fixes this, close.

## Acceptance criteria

- `reconcile.py` `disk_folders()` counts a folder that has EITHER `plan.md` OR `issue-body.md`; a folder with only `issue-body.md` plus a matching ACTIVE README row no longer emits `row-no-folder` drift (add a fixture folder with only `issue-body.md`, assert reconcile exits clean).
- `sync-bodies.py` classifies and diffs folders keyed on `issue-body.md` presence: a staged `issue-body.md` differing from its live GitHub issue is reported (today 0 folders are compared when no `plan.md` exists).
- reconcile output distinguishes `plan.md missing` (warn) from `folder missing` (drift).
- `plans-README.md` documents a state for pre-plan (issue-body-only) rows, or blesses the prose-list pattern; a fresh desk with only staged bodies reconciles clean.

## Dependencies & gates

- **Blocks on:** nothing. Self-contained fix under `primitives-core/skills/planning-desk/scripts/_utils/`.
- **Gates:** `make ci` green + `targets/` regenerated via `make build` (planning-desk scripts are distributed primitives; never hand-edit `targets/`). `project-workflow` plugin version bump. No roster schema change.

> Verified against plugin source 0.2.4 (filed against 0.1.0): defect confirmed still present at `reconcile.py:122-125` and `sync-bodies.py:32`.

> **Origin:** the #24 loadability smoke's first run. The opencode agent transform passed CC frontmatter through verbatim and opencode 1.17 rejected it at load — the interim fix (PR for #24) DROPS the `tools:` key, which loses permission narrowing. Owner-ruled 2026-07-02: drop for now, redesign the baseline as the real fix.

## Problem

`primitives-core/` uses **Claude Code's formats as the base format**, and `translate.py` transforms CC → each target. That works for prose (skills) but breaks down wherever vendors have *semantically different* config surfaces:

- **`tools:`** — CC uses an allowlist (`tools: Read, Grep`); opencode uses a per-tool boolean map that toggles against defaults, so a converted list loads but does not narrow. Currently dropped in the opencode transform (agents get default toolset — widening documented in the transform docstring).
- **env interpolation** — our mcp fragments carry `"${VAR}"` (CC style); opencode does NOT substitute `${VAR}` (its form is `{env:VAR}`), so generated opencode `environment` values are passed literally. Latent bug, same family.
- **frontmatter dialects** — CC parses agent frontmatter leniently; opencode strictly (two source agents with raw multiline descriptions loaded in CC but were silently dropped by opencode until normalized).

## Direction (owner-ruled)

Develop an **agnostic base format** for primitives plus an explicit **cross-vendor mapping layer** (tool ids, permission semantics, env interpolation, frontmatter dialect), instead of CC-as-baseline.

**Research first:** someone has likely already solved cross-CLI agent/config portability in an open-source tool — survey the space (agent format converters, multi-tool dotfile managers for coding agents, e.g. the ecosystems around AGENTS.md, opencode plugins, aider/goose/codex config layers) before inventing a schema.

## Deliverables

- A — survey of prior art for cross-vendor agent/tool/config mapping; recommendation memo (adopt / adapt / build).
- B — proposed base-format spec for the primitive types we translate (agents first; skills are already near-portable), with the vendor mapping tables (tool ids, permission semantics, env interpolation).
- C — migration plan for `primitives-core/` + `translate.py` (per-type, incremental; drift guards keep working throughout).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `tools:` narrowing intent survives translation to opencode (or the spec explicitly records it as unsupported per vendor, surfaced in the build report — no silent widening).
- [ ] mcp env interpolation renders in each vendor's own syntax.
- [ ] `make smoke` green across the board after migration.

## Dependencies & gates

- Depends on: #24 (the smoke that detects these regressions) — merged first.
- `make ci` aggregate: fires on any translate.py/roster change.

## Out of scope

- Runtime shims or wrappers — this stays a static translation service.

> **Tracking:** #48, from Henry's 2026-07-02 notes (`_meta/NOTE.md`). Inventory every "frontend" skill/agent/plugin across the roster and the workbench, and produce a curation plan down to a deliberate core set.

## Problem

The frontend surface has accumulated too many overlapping drafts, with no single view of what exists or which items are meant to survive. Today it spans at least two repos and nine bundles:

- **Roster** (`primitives-core.yaml`): `carbon-builder` (line 62), `obsidian-chat-ui` (line 403), `react-doctor` (line 513), `shadcn` (line 563, also a pending sourced-origin flip under #31).
- **Workbench** (`REGISTRY.md`): `carbon-webapp-team` (line 11, has commands/ to fold), `design-system-toolkit` (line 15, client-token blocker), `frontend-quality-guard` (line 17, client-token blocker), `style-canon` (line 25, client-token blocker), `webapp-designer` (line 27, parked — 8 skills + 6 agents + 3 MCP, "decompose on promotion").

Henry's directive (2026-07-02): "inventory all the frontend skills/agents/plugins and make a plan to curate to a core set. there are way too many drafts." No issue currently owns this; the workbench rows each carry individual blockers but nothing looks at the set as a whole, so overlap (e.g. carbon-builder vs carbon-webapp-team, shadcn vs webapp-designer internals, design-system-toolkit vs style-canon) is invisible.

## Deliverables

- A — **Inventory**: one document (suggested: `_meta/plans/frontend-extenders-curation/plan.md`, or a workbench `docs/` note if the gate process prefers it there) listing EVERY frontend skill/agent/plugin across `primitives-core.yaml`, workbench `REGISTRY.md`, and any live-config stragglers (`~/.claude/skills`, plugin caches), each with type, home, status, and what it actually covers.
- B — **Overlap map**: which items duplicate or subsume each other (the two carbon bundles; shadcn vs webapp-designer's internals; design-system-toolkit vs style-canon).
- C — **Curation plan**: the named target core set, plus a disposition for every other item (keep / merge-into / demote / retire), each with a one-line rationale. Executions become follow-on issues; this issue delivers the plan only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every frontend item in `primitives-core.yaml` and workbench `REGISTRY.md` appears exactly once in the inventory with a disposition — grep of the inventory against both manifests finds no frontend item missing.
- [ ] The plan names the core set explicitly and every non-core item has a stated disposition and rationale.
- [ ] Follow-on issues are filed (or explicitly declared unnecessary) for each merge/demote/retire disposition.

## Dependencies & gates

- Soft dependency on #31 (Q-13 batch triage) — dispositions written there inform, but do not block, the inventory.
- No repo gates fire for this issue itself (report-only; no `primitives-core/` or `targets/` edits). Roster drift guard (`make check`) and targets drift guard (`make build-check`) fire on the follow-on execution issues.

## Out of scope

- Executing any merge/retire/demote — follow-on issues.
- Non-frontend curation (the general Q-13 pass is #31).
title: feat: inventory the frontend extenders and curate to a core set

> **Tracking:** owner ruling 2026-07-02 during the #40 intake (recorded at `_meta/plans/docs-planning-standard/plan.md`, open question 6, RESOLVED). Relates to #40; sibling of standards fixes #34/#35.

## Problem

The PLANS frontmatter audit and the staged-body sync tool contradict each other, so a staged `issue-body.md` cannot satisfy both:

- `repo-compliance-audit/scripts/audit.py:318-327` scopes PLANS-01..06 over every `*.md` under `_meta/plans/` (recursive), excluding only `README.md` and `_`-prefixed path components — so a staged `<slug>/issue-body.md` is REQUIRED to carry frontmatter.
- `_meta/plans/_utils/sync-bodies.py:67` diffs the staged file RAW against the live GitHub issue body (no frontmatter stripping) — so any frontmatter on a staged body reads as permanent phantom drift.

Live consequence: the (now archived) staged body for #41 carried no frontmatter and would have gapped on PLANS-01..06 at the next audit, despite being exactly the publishable body.

**Owner ruling (2026-07-02): issue bodies are exempt from the frontmatter requirements.** A staged `issue-body.md` carries the raw publishable body; the exemption is implemented on the audit side and `sync-bodies.py` stays raw.

## Deliverables

- A — `audit.py`: add `issue-body.md` to the PLANS scope exclusions (the filename filter at `repo-compliance-audit/scripts/audit.py:327`).
- B — Standard prose: state the exemption in the PLANS scope paragraph of `repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md` and in `repo-meta-structure/references/planning-docs.md` (frontmatter-schema scope).
- C — Test: `tests/test_audit.py` fixture with a frontmatter-less `<slug>/issue-body.md` (no PLANS gap) alongside a frontmatter-less `<slug>/plan.md` (still gaps).

## Acceptance criteria

- Audit of a fixture repo containing `_meta/plans/x/issue-body.md` with NO frontmatter reports zero PLANS gaps for that file.
- The same fixture's `plan.md` without frontmatter still gaps on PLANS-01..06 (exemption is filename-scoped, not folder-wide).
- checklist.md's PLANS scope prose and planning-docs.md name the exemption identically (no divergent wording between the two).
- `make ci` green; `make build-check` clean after regeneration.

## Dependencies & gates

- Fires: `make ci` (always); targets drift guard `make build-check` (edits under `primitives-core/` regenerate `targets/`).
- Does not fire: roster drift guard (no primitive added/removed/renamed); naming taxonomy; yamllint/actionlint.
- No ordering dependency on #40 (touches the PLANS scope, not the DOCS rows), but both edit `checklist.md` — whichever lands second rebases trivially.

## Out of scope

Changes to `sync-bodies.py` (stays raw per the ruling); the DOCS-xx rows (#40); retro-fitting frontmatter onto archived staged bodies.
title: fix: exempt issue-body.md from the PLANS frontmatter audit (owner ruling 2026-07-02)

Two more Gate-2 pilot findings (raptorgpt-agents PR #541 review pass, 2026-07-02) — template defects in the repo-meta-structure standard's assets, surfaced only when the scaffold ran against a repo with its own conventions:

1. **Issue templates hardcode label names.** The feature template applies `enhancement`; the pilot repo's taxonomy uses `feature` (fixed in-PR there). The epic template references an `epic` label that may not exist in the target repo at all. The templates assume a label taxonomy the scaffold neither creates nor verifies (labels are declared in `_meta/mise-en-place.yml` for github-project-board, never provisioned).
2. **Duplicate-reviewer blind spot.** The audit's GH-08 checks for `.github/workflows/claude-review.yml` by filename; the pilot repo already had an equivalent review workflow under a different name ("PR Review with Progress Tracking"), so the scaffold added a second reviewer — two AI reviews and double token spend per push until deduped by hand. Also: the pilot's pre-existing workflow had a concurrency/cancel-stale setting worth adopting in the standard's template.

## Deliverables
- Templates: either derive labels from the manifest's `gh_issue_labels` (with a documented default set) or ship label-less templates; document the constraint in the standard.
- Audit/scaffold: content-probe for existing claude-review-equivalent workflows (e.g. grep for the action name across `.github/workflows/`) and report a CONFLICT/MANUAL instead of creating a duplicate.
- Consider `concurrency` + cancel-in-progress in the claude-review template.

## Acceptance criteria
- Re-running the pilot sequence on raptorgpt-agents (post-#541) plans zero duplicate workflows and no unknown-label templates; `make ci` green.

Refs: raptorgpt-agents#541 (commit 5), raptorgpt-agents#542 (repo-side label reconcile); sibling finding #38 (gitignore-swallow).
title: scaffold templates: hardcoded labels + duplicate-reviewer blind spot (Gate-2 pilot findings)

> **Tracking:** #TBD, found 2026-07-02 while writing `docs/plugins/project-workflow.md` (the plugin user guide). The board skills instruct running three helper scripts that the built plugin does not ship.

### What's wrong

The three board helper scripts — `board-export.py`, `board-fields.py`, `board-apply.py` — are load-bearing for four project-workflow primitives, all of which reference them as if they ship with the plugin:

- `primitives-core/skills/github-project-board/SKILL.md:256` — "the three scripts live at the plugin root `scripts/`; run them from the plugin directory" (usage examples at :281-286).
- `primitives-core/skills/board-triage/SKILL.md:29-32` — "Run the toolkit (scripts live at the plugin root `scripts/`)"; apply step at :51-52.
- `primitives-core/skills/board-reporting/SKILL.md:24-25` — snapshot step, "(scripts live at the plugin root `scripts/`)".
- `primitives-core/agents/board-analyst.md:46-47` — "Use `Bash` only to run `board-export.py`/`board-fields.py` (reads)".

But the scripts exist nowhere in this repo — not in any `primitives-core/skills/*/scripts/` dir (`primitives-core/skills/github-project-board/` contains only `SKILL.md`) and not in the built plugin (`targets/claude-code/plugins/project-workflow/` contains only `.claude-plugin/`, `agents/`, `skills/`; there is no plugin-root `scripts/`). The only surviving copies are in the frozen pre-migration repo: `hsb3-custom-plugins/plugins/github-projects-board-management/scripts/`.

Expected: a fresh install of the plugin can run the export -> analyze -> apply loop the skills describe. Observed: every quoted `scripts/board-*.py` invocation fails with file-not-found; a session must fall back to reconstructing the `gh`/GraphQL calls by hand.

Precedent that the fix is mechanically easy: skill-level script dirs already ship whole — `primitives-core/skills/planning-desk/scripts/` and `primitives-core/skills/repo-compliance-audit/scripts/` are bundled by the build's `copytree` (`scripts/translate.py:164`). There is no plugin-root asset mechanism in the build today.

### Repro

1. Install the plugin: `claude plugin marketplace add hsb3/dotfiles-agents && claude plugin install project-workflow@dotfiles-agents`.
2. Ask for a board snapshot per `board-triage` step 1: `scripts/board-export.py -o <owner> -n <number> --out board-snapshot.json` from the plugin directory.
3. File not found — `ls ~/.claude/plugins/cache/dotfiles-agents/project-workflow/0.1.0/` shows no `scripts/` dir.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `board-export.py`, `board-fields.py`, `board-apply.py` exist under `primitives-core/` (home per the open decision below) and appear in the built plugin after `make build`.
- [ ] Every script reference in the four primitives above points at the shipped location; `rg "plugin root .scripts/" primitives-core/` returns zero hits.
- [ ] From a fresh plugin install, `python3 <shipped-path>/board-export.py --help` exits 0 (scripts stay stdlib + `gh` only, per the toolkit contract).
- [ ] `make ci` green (targets drift guard regenerated, roster guard unchanged or updated per the decision).
- [ ] The "Known gap (v0.1.0)" callout in `docs/plugins/project-workflow.md` is removed or rewritten in the same PR.

### Dependencies & gates

- Open owner decision - where the scripts live:
  - **(A) recommended:** `primitives-core/skills/github-project-board/scripts/` (the skill that owns the loop); board-triage / board-reporting / board-analyst reference it via the plugin cache path or `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/github-project-board/scripts/`. Zero build changes; also travels in raw (non-plugin) skill deploys to opencode.
  - **(B):** teach `scripts/translate.py` a plugin-level `scripts/` assembly step to match the current skill wording. More build machinery; does not help raw deploys.
- Gates that fire: **targets drift guard** (`make build-check`; any `primitives-core/` edit) and the **CI aggregate** (`make ci`). Roster drift guard fires only if option B adds a new primitive/attribute. Naming taxonomy: advisory only (no new primitive under option A). yamllint/actionlint do NOT fire (no YAML/workflow edits under option A).
- Source of the scripts to migrate: `hsb3-custom-plugins/plugins/github-projects-board-management/scripts/` (frozen repo; copy, do not link).
title: fix: board helper scripts referenced by the board skills are not bundled in the built plugin

> **Tracking:** #40, from the dotfiles-agents-cowork desk (standards-curation thread; follows
> the project-workflow conformance pass, `_meta/plans/project-workflow-conformance.md`). Extend
> the repo meta-structure standard so `docs/` has enforced minimums — a decisions/ ADR
> directory and a CHARTER.md canonical page — then bring this repo to conformance and refresh
> the installed plugin so the standards skills actually reach the machine.

## Problem

The repo meta-structure standard audits everything around `docs/` but nothing inside it. The
checklist's only docs row is ROOT-08, `path-exists: docs/`
(`primitives-core/skills/repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md:77`) — an empty `docs/`
directory passes. There is no DOCS row family, no ADR-directory requirement, and no
canonical-page requirement, even though:

- The standard itself leans on decisions it can't point at: checklist rows cite "the
  skills-over-commands decision" (CLAUDE-07) and "the hooks-as-script-plus-config decision"
  (HOOK-01 note), but this repo has no `docs/decisions/` to hold them —
  `docs/` today is `CHARTER.md`, `images/`, `sops/` only. This repo would gap against the
  very rows it should define.
- The best worked example, `hsb3/ra-platform`, carries the shape the standard should name:
  `docs/README.md` (orientation + docs-vs-`_meta/` boundary), `docs/decisions/` with
  `README.md` (append-only convention + index) and `0000-template.md` plus 29 sequential
  ADRs. It is a reference point, not necessarily the ultimate standard — the required set is
  an open decision below.
- Conversely ra-platform has no `docs/CHARTER.md` while this repo does (with the precedence
  line "if anything anywhere disagrees with this page, this page wins",
  `docs/CHARTER.md:9`) — neither exemplar passes the union today, which is exactly why the
  minimum needs to be written down as rows, not inferred from examples.

Separately, the standard's enforcement skills never reached the installed plugin: the roster
assigns `repo-meta-structure`, `repo-compliance-audit`, `mise-en-place-scaffold`, and
`memory-taxonomy` to `plugins: [project-workflow]` (`primitives-core.yaml`) and the built
target carries them (`targets/claude-code/plugins/project-workflow/skills/`), but
`plugins.yaml` still says `version: "0.1.0"` — the same version as the installed cache
(`~/.claude/plugins/cache/dotfiles-agents/project-workflow/0.1.0/`), which predates the
standards work and contains only 9 skills. Without a version bump the plugin manager sees no
update, so the audit/scaffold skills are invisible on the machines that need them.

## Deliverables

- **A — DOCS-xx checklist rows + layout guidance.** New `## docs/ minimum planning docs`
  section in `repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md` (rows DOCS-01..05: `docs/README.md`,
  `docs/CHARTER.md`, `docs/decisions/`, `docs/decisions/README.md`,
  `docs/decisions/0000-template.md` — all `path-exists`, so zero audit-script change), plus a
  `docs/` section in `references/layout.md` stating the minimums and marking deeper taxonomy
  (design workspaces, operations, api) as per-repo variance, not rows.
- **B — Scaffold assets + mapping.** `repo-meta-structure/assets/docs/README.md` and
  `assets/docs/decisions/{README.md,0000-template.md}` (modeled on ra-platform); a `docs/`
  branch in `mise-en-place-scaffold/scripts/scaffold.py::template_source`; `docs/CHARTER.md`
  added to `AUTHORED_FILES` (flagged manual, never scaffolded — it is the canonical page).
- **C — Tests.** Extend `tests/test_audit.py` + `tests/test_scaffold.py` to cover the new
  rows, assets, and the CHARTER authored-file behavior.
- **D — Apply to this repo.** Run the scaffold, author the `docs/README.md` index, seed
  `docs/decisions/` with the template + README and backfill the already-load-bearing
  decisions the standard cites (skills-over-commands; hooks-as-script-plus-config;
  externals-tracked-not-vendored). Re-audit to 0 GAP.
- **E — Plugin refresh.** Bump `project-workflow` in `plugins.yaml`, `make build`, update the
  installed plugin so the four standards skills (and the new DOCS content) reach the machine.
  Coordinate with #27 (v2 rename/bump) — if #27 lands in the same window, E folds into it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `python3 <plugin>/skills/repo-compliance-audit/scripts/audit.py` on this repo reports the
  five DOCS rows and exits 0 GAP (or every remaining gap named + justified in the commit).
- The same audit run on a bare fixture repo reports DOCS-01..05 as GAP (rows actually fire).
- `mise-en-place-scaffold --plan` on a repo missing `docs/` plans the templated files and
  reports `docs/CHARTER.md` as manual/authored; `--apply` is additive-only (no overwrites).
- `docs/decisions/` in this repo contains `README.md`, `0000-template.md`, and at least the
  three backfilled ADRs, numbered sequentially from 0001.
- `make ci` green (existing 158 tests + new ones); `make build-check` clean after regeneration.
- The installed `project-workflow` plugin cache version is greater than 0.1.0 and contains
  `repo-compliance-audit`, `repo-meta-structure`, `mise-en-place-scaffold`, `memory-taxonomy`.

## Dependencies & gates

- **Fires:** `make ci` (always); targets drift guard `make build-check` (edits under
  `primitives-core/` regenerate `targets/` — never hand-edit `targets/`).
- **Does not fire:** roster drift guard `make check` (no primitive added/removed/renamed —
  this is content inside existing skills); naming taxonomy (no new primitive); yamllint /
  actionlint (no workflow edits).
- **Ordering:** #27 renames all project-workflow primitives under `pw-`; whichever of the two
  lands second carries the mechanical path rebase. Related standards fixes #34 (gitkeep clone
  survival) and #35 (`_archive` naming) are adjacent but non-overlapping.

## Out of scope

Applying the DOCS rows to `dotfiles-agents-workbench` and other repos (follow-up pass, same
mechanism); a full ADR backfill of this repo's history beyond the three load-bearing
decisions; any new check *types* in the audit vocabulary; deeper `docs/` taxonomy rows
(workspace dirs stay layout guidance); GitHub-side provisioning.

> **Origin:** surfaced by the #22 test suite. `translate.py` reads files with `open(...).read()` and never closes them; the new tests raise `ResourceWarning`s (currently silenced in the runner via `-W ignore::ResourceWarning`).

## Problem

`scripts/translate.py` opens files without closing them in several hot paths -- e.g. the parsers (`:56`, `:109`), `sha256_path` (`:185`), `skill_display_title` (`:226`), and others use `open(path).read()` / `for raw in open(path)`. Under the unit tests this surfaces as `ResourceWarning: unclosed file`, which `make test` currently hides with `-W ignore::ResourceWarning`. The leak is benign in the short-lived CLI but is a latent correctness/style issue and forces the test runner to suppress a whole warning class.

## Deliverables

- A -- wrap every read in `translate.py` in a `with` block (or a small `read_text(path)` / `read_bytes(path)` helper) so no handle leaks.
- B -- drop the `-W ignore::ResourceWarning` suppression from the `make test` target once the leaks are gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` passes with **zero** `ResourceWarning` (warnings-as-errors).
- [ ] `make test` no longer needs `-W ignore::ResourceWarning`.
- [ ] `make ci` stays green and `targets/` is byte-identical (pure refactor, no output change).

## Dependencies & gates

- `make ci` aggregate: FIRES -- the targets drift guard must stay green (no rendered-output change).
- Roster / naming gates: do NOT fire (no primitive or plugin touched).

## Out of scope

- Any behavior or output change in the translation service (this is a pure resource-handling refactor).
- Broader refactors of `translate.py` beyond closing file handles.
title: chore: close file handles in translate.py (drop ResourceWarning suppression)

body:
> **Origin:** Henry ("this repo needs some test/qa procedures"), 2026-06-29. Add a correctness layer on top of the existing drift guards so render/transform bugs are caught, not just inconsistencies.

## Problem

The only automated checks are two **drift guards** run by `make ci` (`Makefile:21`): `check_roster.py` (roster matches disk) and `translate.py --check` (committed `targets/` equals a fresh rebuild). They prove **consistency**, not **correctness** -- a bug in a renderer emits wrong-but-consistent output that passes `make ci` clean, because the guard only diffs the rebuild against the committed copy (`translate.py:594`).

Concretely uncovered today: the pure render/transform/parse functions in `scripts/translate.py` (the `mcp_to_*` renderers `:242/:258/:275`, `transform_agent_opencode` `:189`, the five stdlib parsers `:54/:80/:107/:122/:143`) have zero unit tests; nothing validates a source primitive's content (a skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter, an mcp spec's required fields per transport); nothing checks a generated artifact against its target's real schema (CMA `name`+`model`, opencode `mcp` shape, `marketplace.json` keys); there is no determinism assertion and no secret-hygiene gate; and there is no test infra at all (`tests/`, `make test`, framework, CI lane). The suite is intentionally **zero-install** (`translate.py:14`), so any solution must stay stdlib-only in CI.

## Deliverables

- A -- test harness (`tests/`, `make test`, CI step) + unit tests for the pure functions: the three `mcp_to_*` renderers (stdio AND http), the transforms (`transform_agent_opencode`, `agent_system`, `skill_display_title`), the five parsers (real-file round-trip + edge cases), `_list`, `sha256_path`. Fixtures live under `tests/`, never `primitives-core/`.
- B -- `scripts/validate_primitives.py` + `make validate`: content validation the drift guards skip (skill/agent frontmatter; mcp spec `transport`+`command`/`url`; `${VAR}` placeholders not literals; `origin`/`targets`/`summary` roster cross-checks). Folded into `make ci`.
- C -- `tests/test_targets.py`: generated-artifact schema checks (CMA `name`+`model`+`system`; `*/mcp/*.json` shape; `*.upload.json`; `marketplace.json`/`plugin.json` keys) + invariants (build-twice determinism; secret-hygiene scan of `targets/`).
- D -- (DEFERRED, opt-in `make smoke`, not in required CI) loadability against the real tools: CMA payloads vs the pinned `BetaManagedAgentsCreateAgentParams`; opencode/CC config-parse smoke that skips when the tool is absent.

Full build detail, file scope, and landing order: `_meta/plans/test-qa-procedures/plan.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `make test` runs green with **zero `pip install`**; CI runs it.
- [ ] Each `mcp_to_*` renderer has a stdio AND an http assertion; `transform_agent_opencode` is asserted to preserve a multi-line `description` byte-for-byte.
- [ ] A deliberately mutated expectation makes the suite FAIL (the tests can actually catch a regression).
- [ ] `validate_primitives.py` exits non-zero on a broken fixture (skill missing `description`; mcp spec missing `transport`) and zero on the real tree; it is part of `make ci`.
- [ ] The determinism test builds twice and asserts byte-identical output; the secret scan passes on current `targets/` and FAILS on a fixture carrying a literal token.
- [ ] Every `targets/claude-agents/agents/*.json` is asserted to carry `name`+`model`.

## Dependencies & gates

- `make ci` (aggregate, required): FIRES -- this adds `test`+`validate` lanes into it.
- Roster drift guard: does NOT fire, PROVIDED fixtures live under `tests/` not `primitives-core/` (else `check_roster.py:55` flags them as orphans).
- Targets drift guard: does NOT fire -- no `primitives-core/`/roster/config edits; tests only READ `targets/`.
- `actionlint`/`yamllint`: FIRES -- editing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to add the lane.
- Naming taxonomy: does NOT fire -- adds only `scripts/` + `tests/`, no primitive/plugin.
- Owner decisions RESOLVED (2026-06-29): framework = stdlib `unittest` (zero-install); separate `make test` + `make validate`, both in `make ci`; validation as a `scripts/` guard, unit tests in `tests/`; **defer D** to a follow-up; no new gate label. See the plan's "Owner decisions (RESOLVED)".

## Out of scope

- Real end-to-end loading inside Claude Code / opencode / the CMA API (that is D, deferred and opt-in).
- The skill/plugin clone-at-build externals path (unrelated, separately tracked).
- Reformatting or refactoring `translate.py` beyond what testability requires.
- Any new runtime dependency in the required CI lane (the suite stays zero-install).
title: harden: test/QA procedures — correctness layer over the drift guards

> **Tracking:** #6, the residual after the Phase 3 MVP translation service shipped (#17). Build the two adapters the MVP deliberately deferred: the Claude managed-agents (CMA) renderer and the mcp renderer.

## Problem

The translation service shipped as an MVP (#17): `scripts/translate.py` renders **skills** (native copy) and **agents** (opencode transform) and assembles the **Claude Code marketplace**, gated by `make ci`. Two capability cells in `primitives-core-translation-config.yaml` are configured but **not implemented** — they are recorded as skips, not rendered:

- **claude-agents (CMA)** — `scripts/translate.py:290-301` records every claude-agents target as `{"capability": "render", "reason": "claude-agents (CMA) adapter deferred (post-MVP)", "skipped": true}`. So `targets/claude-agents/` is empty (only `.gitkeep`) and the results lock carries 71 deferred skips. The adapters `cma_skill_upload` / `cma_agent_create` named at `primitives-core-translation-config.yaml:43,48` don't exist. The CMA contract is already pinned (CANON "Resolved — managed-agents (CMA) contract": `POST /v1/skills` multipart with `SKILL.md` at root; `POST /v1/agents` with `BetaManagedAgentsCreateAgentParams`).
- **mcp render** — `primitives-core-translation-config.yaml:50-53` configures `mcp_to_claude` / `mcp_to_opencode` / `mcp_to_cma`, but `primitives-core/mcp/` is **empty** (only `.gitkeep`), and the roster has **zero** `type: mcp` entries. There is nothing to render and nothing to test the renderer against — mcp render is blocked on a first mcp primitive existing.

This is the deferred half of #6; the MVP half (skills/agents/CC marketplace + drift guard) is done and closed via #17.

## Deliverables

- **A — CMA adapter** in `scripts/translate.py` (replaces the deferred-skip block at `:290-301`). Emit static, deterministic artifacts under `targets/claude-agents/`:
  - per skill targeting claude-agents: a build-sheet/manifest describing the `POST /v1/skills` multipart upload (the skill folder is uploaded as-is; `name`/`description` extracted from `SKILL.md`).
  - per agent: a `BetaManagedAgentsCreateAgentParams` payload JSON (`name`, `model`, `system` = agent body, `tools[]`, `skills[]` refs, `mcp_servers[]`).
  - record real (non-skip) results in `primitives-core-translation-results.json`; extend `make build-check`/CI to guard `targets/claude-agents/`.
- **B — mcp render adapter** (`mcp_to_claude` / `mcp_to_opencode` / `mcp_to_cma` in `scripts/translate.py`) — implement against the neutral `primitives-core/mcp/<name>.json` spec, **gated on a first mcp primitive existing** (see Dependencies). Until then, the cells stay `render`-configured but unexercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `targets/claude-agents/` is non-empty after `make build`: contains a CMA payload/manifest for every roster entry whose `targets` includes `claude-agents` (71 today).
- [ ] `primitives-core-translation-results.json` shows `claude-agents` entries with `"skipped": false` and a `destination` + `sha256` (grep for `"claude-agents (CMA) adapter deferred"` returns zero hits).
- [ ] Each generated agent payload is valid JSON and carries the required `BetaManagedAgentsCreateAgentParams` fields `name` + `model` (verifiable: `python3 -c` loads each and asserts the keys).
- [ ] Build is deterministic — `make build` twice produces byte-identical `targets/claude-agents/` + lock (the existing run-twice check extended to the new target).
- [ ] `make ci` (drift guard) green: `translate.py --check` covers `targets/claude-agents/`.
- [ ] **B (mcp):** when a `type: mcp` primitive is added to the roster, `make build` renders it to each target without a code change to the adapters; `make ci` stays green. (If no mcp primitive is added in this issue, B is split to a follow-up — see Out of scope.)

## Dependencies & gates

- **Blocks on:** Deliverable B blocks on a first `type: mcp` primitive existing in `primitives-core/mcp/` + the roster — there is none today, so B cannot be exercised or tested until one lands. A is unblocked (real inputs exist).
- **Gates that fire:** `make ci` (the roster + targets drift guards) — always; **targets drift guard** (`make build-check`, fix with `make build`) — this changes generated `targets/` output, so the lock must be regenerated in the same PR; `yamllint`/`actionlint` if the config or CI workflow changes.
- **Gates that do NOT fire:** roster↔disk (`make check`) only matters if primitives change — A/B add no primitives (B's mcp primitive, if added, would trigger it); no DB / infra / API-codegen gates in this repo.
- **Contract to keep in sync:** the CMA contract in CANON "Resolved — managed-agents (CMA) contract" — if the adapter deviates from the pinned `POST /v1/skills` / `POST /v1/agents` shapes, amend that note in the same change.

## Out of scope

- **Live API calls / uploading** to the managed-agents API — the adapter emits **static payloads/build-sheets** only; actually POSTing them is a deploy-time concern (dotfiles-bootstrap), not the translation build.
- Model-id mapping for CMA agent payloads beyond carrying the agent's stated tier (the opencode transform already omits model; same simplification applies unless a mapping is decided).
- If no mcp primitive is created here, **Deliverable B becomes a tracked follow-up** ("render the first mcp primitive") rather than blocking A from closing #6's CMA half.
